rationale: When the AMF is killed and restarted after the NAS security context is set up, it loses that context and fails to decode the ciphered NAS message container in the UE's GUTI Registration Request, instead of re-authenticating. One quick AMF restart triggers it (the 30 s sleep is only time to restart by hand).

After an AMF reboot it has forgotten all UEs, and it drops the Service Request of a UE that still thinks it is registered instead of sending Service Reject #9, so the UE never reconnects. One immediate AMF restart triggers it.

With an aggressive 10 ms heartbeat and timeout, the UPF stays up but heartbeats are falsely missed; the SMF re-associates, but late responses make the PFCP receive goroutine block on a channel send, so re-association never completes (no UE needed). It depends on late responses to timed-out transactions under heartbeat timer pressure, which a crash-stop UPF would not produce, so it is judged outside the extended model.

After the gNB CU/DU is killed and restarted (with SCTP shutdown and a new NGSetup), the SMF intermittently reports the UE's previous IP as still in use, and the UE cannot get a PDU session until free5GC is restarted. The repro uses one CPE.

An interceptor drops the UPF's PFCP Session Establishment Responses. On the PFCP-timeout reject path, the SMF never releases the SM context or its UE IP, and repeated attempts exhaust a /29 pool. Judgement: stopping the UPF for less than heartbeat give-up while a session is being established would produce the same PFCP timeout, so the extended model covers it.

If the NRF is down, the OAuth GetTokenCtx call in SM context create fails, and the SMF returns an empty 200 without releasing the SMContext. One request is enough to leak one context. It needs oauth enabled and an SM context create that arrives during the NRF outage, which the extended model's NRF crash/restart covers.

The UPF stays associated but ignores PFCP Session Deletion (a stub in the PoC), so a duplicate PDU session create takes SessionReleaseFailed and orphans one SMContext, UE IP and 4 TEIDs per UE retry (single SUPI/PSI). Judged reproducible by UPF crash-stop with downtime below heartbeat give-up (deletion times out while the association stays up); past give-up, association release would sweep the orphan, hence the timer dependence.

A duplicate PDU session request runs local release while the UPF is unreachable (or rejects/times out the N4 deletion), so SessionReleaseFailed skips CHARGING_RELEASE and leaves a zombie SMContext. Covered by UPF crash-stop with downtime during the release (no immediate restart needed); the charging leak occurs whether or not heartbeat give-up later sweeps the context. The PoC forced the failure in a unit harness.

Crafted Handover messages panic NGAP workers inside the still-running AMF, and dead workers are never restarted. After 4 panics on different UE IDs the repro reaches Worker 0, which all NGSetupRequests go to, and new gNBs get no response. The trigger is an in-process panic, not an NF crash/restart; a single panic that lands on Worker 0 would be enough.

After an AMF pod restart ('kubectl delete pod'), the SMF's per-SMContext CommunicationClient and its NRF cache keep the old AMF pod IP, so N1N2MessageTransfer hangs and PDU session establishment fails until the SMF restarts. A single immediate restart is enough, but only when the restarted AMF comes back at a new address (K8s pod IP).

Every SMF start bumps a persistent smfCount, which offsets UE IPs by (count-1)*5000. On a /24 pool, a single 'kubectl rollout restart' already hands a re-attaching UE an address outside the pool, which breaks downlink. Config preconditions: enableDBStore=true and the SMF doing the IP allocation.

Restarting the EPC SGW (mapped to other) makes it lose UE state, so the MME's Create Session Request with an old TEID hits ASSERT !(sgw_ue) and the UE cannot re-attach. The failed entity is EPC, so both models exclude it.

With the SGs interface (MSC/VLR peer, other) configured but unreachable, the EPC MME (other) restarts as soon as a UE connects. This is EPC with an unreachable but alive peer, so both models exclude it.

After the NRF restarts with an empty cache, a third-party NF's heartbeat gets 404 and the NF re-registers with a large PUT. The NRF's HTTP/2 large-message handling bug then closes the socket or crashes the NRF. A single NRF restart triggers it, but the maintainer notes Open5GS's own NFs do not send such a message.

When a gNB with 40+ connected UEs drops its N2/SCTP connection, the AMF hits a FATAL on the sockinfo assertion. It does not happen with 14 UEs, and the fix enlarged the memory pool, so the bug needs pool pressure.

The SMF crashes on an invalid Downlink Data Service Information in a PFCP Session Report. This happens when a UE reconnects after a context release (Initial Context Setup Response), so the trigger is a UE procedure, not an injected fault. The leftover state after the SMF's automatic restart (all NFs had to be restarted) is a side effect; the confirmed fix targets the crash.

When the user-plane host (UPF/SGW-U) crashes and restarts, it loses all PFCP state while the SMF/SGW-C keep their sessions. Attached UEs lose traffic and detaches fail until the whole control plane is restarted. One UPF crash-restart is enough.

The reporter saw stale SMF session counts after stopping the gNB and UEs, which the maintainer said is by design. The confirmed fix is a BSF binding keyed only on S-NSSAI+DNN: when a second UE deregisters, no PFCP session delete is sent. That needs two UEs and no NF failure.
The gNB sends an NG Reset in reply to a UE Context Release Command, and the AMF crashes. A single NG Reset from the RAN, racing an ongoing UE release, triggers it.

A host carrying most UPFs/SGW-Us was shut down. On SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT, the SMF asserted on sess->sm_context_ref, because of a reused 'next' iterator and a node freed after the N4 timeout. The UPF has to stay down past heartbeat give-up, and per the comments a session establishment was in flight at that moment. UE count is inferred (production load).

With two UPFs (HA), UPF1 is killed and stays down while the UE is CM_IDLE; on the next Service Request the SMF does not trigger PDU session re-establishment on UPF2 (it even confirms activation on the dead UPF1). The SMF must first declare UPF1 dead via PFCP heartbeat, so this is downtime past give-up, not an immediate restart.

The upg-vpp UPF drops the UE contexts and the PFCP association without any reported restart. It then answers 'No established PFCP Association', and the SMF never re-associates until it is restarted itself. Inferred: the thread does not say why the UPF lost the association; a crash-restart would have been detected through the Recovery Time Stamp.

After a UDR stop/restart, the UDM keeps a stale nf_instance pointer in its sbi_object (a ref-count asymmetry), falls back to nf_instance->client on default port 80, and the UE's re-registration fails. The failed NF is UDR, which is outside the crashable set of both models.

A live UDM (an HTTP/2 server with a 1 s request timeout) sends GOAWAY while 1000 UEs register, and the AMF reportedly keeps using the closed TCP stream. No NF crashes; the maintainer could not reproduce it (curl opens a new connection), and the issue was closed as stale.

In a dual-EPC failover, the whole main EPC (MME, SGW-C/U, PGW-C/U) is taken down with docker compose down, the eNB moves to the local EPC, and then the main EPC comes back. The UE re-attaches but the user plane fails. Several EPC entities restart at once and none is a 5GC NF, so it is outside both models; there is no root-cause discussion in the thread.

A gNB lock/unlock drops and re-establishes SCTP within seconds; a UE re-registering with a fresh SUCI while the old sessions are still being torn down gets a zombie sess_list, so N1N2MessageTransfer returns 400 and SMF sessions and IPs leak on every retry. It races the asynchronous teardown, not a heartbeat or association timer, and depends on UE behaviour (iPhone SUCI rotation).

Each NG-RAN SCTP close after an Identity Request leaks one pre-registered amf_ue in the AMF; the reported symptom (pool exhaustion, rejection with 'control processing overload') needed 1024 repeated cycles. Each cycle is a single gNB SCTP loss, so one fault already leaves one stale amf_ue: n_faults=1 and the extended model covers it via gNB SCTP loss. The visible outage needs pool pressure.

A single GTP-U Error Indication from the SGW-U (EPC, mapped to other) on S5-U makes the SMF/PGW-C silently delete the whole IMS PDN without a Delete Bearer Request to the MME. No NF crash is involved and the entities are EPC, so both models exclude it.

Two GTP-U Error Indications from the SGW-U (EPC, mapped to other) for the same bearer, plus an SGW-C that never answers Delete Bearer, start duplicate deactivations; each Delete Bearer transaction timeout sends its own PFCP remove, and the second response hits ogs_assert(bearer) in the SMF. This is EPC with no NF crash, and it depends on GTP transaction timer expiry.

After request-rate overload (20k UEs at ~500/s) the AMF's HTTP/2 connection to the SMF goes half-dead (TCP up, the SMF application silent), and libcurl keeps reusing it, so every request times out. The peer process stays alive; a crash-stop would close the TCP connection and force a new one, so it would not reproduce this.

The UPF (eUPF) stays up but does not answer some PFCP Session Deletions; if the AMF-side SBI stream is already gone when the deletion transaction gives up, sess_5gc_timeout hits ogs_assert(stream) and the SMF aborts. Judged covered by UPF crash-stop with downtime during a release (same deletion timeout), but it depends on the PFCP give-up timer racing the SBI stream lifetime. It was seen under 600-1100 UE churn but also in pespin's TTCN-3 tests, so a single UE is inferred to suffice.

When the only UPF stops answering heartbeats (TTCN-3 timeout test; full-core repro is 'docker stop upf' for ~36 s), the SMF never releases the UE sessions. The behaviour only appears once the downtime exceeds heartbeat give-up, and the thread shows release versus restoration being decided by heartbeat phase.

Repro: kill open5gs-smfd and let the UPF keep sending heartbeats until t3_holding_duration expires. The UPF only goes back to will_associate and never deletes the SMF's sessions. The bug only shows if the SMF stays down past heartbeat give-up, or never comes back with a new Recovery Time Stamp.

Sequence: 'docker stop upf', wait past heartbeat give-up, then 'docker start upf'. PFCP restoration re-installs sessions that are still mid-release, with the UEs' old IPs, which silently black-holes downlink. The comment shows the bug needs the restart to straddle the give-up window while the N1/N2 release is still in flight; a quick restart where UEs answer promptly does not show it.

While the SMF is down (left down in the PoC), SMF discovery fails and the AMF leaves a pdu_session_context per PSI that is never released; de-registration then stalls TASK_AMF_N1 for 1 s per survivor. This needs SMF downtime spanning the PDU session attempts, not an immediate restart. That discovery fails with no NRF heartbeat expiry (the stopped SMF is absent from the NRF) is inferred.

After 'docker restart oai-gnb' (or NG Reset / SCTP close), release_ngap_context_only() moves UEs to CM-IDLE without starting the mobile reachable timer, so a UE that does not return is never implicitly deregistered. The missing timer is the NAS mobile-reachable timer, not a heartbeat/association timer, and the stale state is present right after one gNB restart.

After 'docker restart oai-smf' the smContextRef counter restarts at 1, so the AMF's stale reference from the old run releases another UE's new PDU session; this needs two UEs, one holding the old ref and one getting the reused ref. The reporters also restarted the UPF, but only to avoid a separate bug (oai-cn5g-upf#41), so one SMF restart is counted as the fault.

After 'docker restart oai-smf', the SMF re-sends Association Setup and the UPF keeps the old association's sessions. The restarted SMF's CP SEIDs (starting from 1 again) collide with the stale sessions, so new sessions are rejected (5GSM #38). One UE that held a session before the restart and asks for a new one afterwards is enough; the reporters used 4.
